Investors are completely risk-neutral across maturities

cards.title: 1. Repo Leverage Machine
cards.subtitle: Financing $20.5B on $7.5B Equity
bulletPoints: Orange County had $7.5B in tax and municipal funds
Borrowed $13B in short-term reverse repo agreements
Built a massive $20.5B leveraged fixed income portfolio

cards.title: 2. The Inverse Floater Bet
cards.subtitle: Betting Interest Rates Would Never Rise
bulletPoints: Invested heavily in inverse floating-rate notes
Yields rose when interest rates fell, but collapsed if rates rose
Funded entirely by rolling overnight and short-term repo debt

cards.title: 3. Fed Tightening Shock
cards.subtitle: Six Rate Hikes in 1994 (+250 bps)
bulletPoints: Federal Reserve raised rates 6 consecutive times from 3% to 5.5%
Short repo borrowing costs surged far above inverse floater yields
Portfolio suffered catastrophic negative carry every single day

cards.title: 4. Margin Collapse & Bankruptcy
cards.subtitle: $1.6 Billion Municipal Liquidation
bulletPoints: Wall Street lenders demanded $1B+ in immediate cash margin calls
County could not meet margin; dealers seized and liquidated collateral
Suffered $1.6B loss and filed largest municipal bankruptcy in US history

scenes.title: The Whole Picture: 8 Core Term Structure Rules

beats.hindi_tts: The complete chapter at a glance: Eight foundational principles governing forward rates and term structure.
beats.en_subtitle: The entire chapter at a glance: Eight core principles of forward rates and term structure.
beats.en_narration: The complete chapter at a glance: Eight foundational principles governing forward rates and term structure.

ui_state.heading: Forward Rates & Term Structure Master Thread
steps: 1. Implied Forward Formula: Continuous forward rate R_F = (R_2*T_2 - R_1*T_1)/(T_2 - T_1) is determined by zero rates.
2. No-Arbitrage Replication: Borrowing for T1 and investing for T2 synthetically replicates a forward loan.
3. FRA Hedging Architecture: Fixed payers receive floating R_M and pay fixed R_K to cap borrowing costs.
4. Advance Settlement Discount: FRAs settling at time T_1 discount payoffs by [1 + R_M*(T_2 - T_1)].
5. Pre-Maturity Valuation: Existing FRAs are valued by discounting the spread between current R_F and contract R_K.
6. Liquidity Preference Reality: Forward rates exceed expected spot rates (R_F > E[R]) by a positive liquidity buffer.
7. Orange County Lesson: Funding long assets with $13B short repo leverage destroyed $1.6B during Fed rate hikes.
8. Interbank Liquidity Freeze: In 2008, commercial paper froze and LIBOR-OIS spread exploded to a record 364 bps.
ui_state.bottomTakeaway: Forward rates represent no-arbitrage break-evens; liquidity preference creates normal upward slope, and FRAs lock future borrowing costs.
